summary: The events sub-resource route audit found that public.event_posts is read and written by two live routes but is created by no file in supabase/migrations/. The only definitions are supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20250120000000_event_social_features.sql (MANIFEST.csv status duplicate_version_noncanonical, in a directory named local-only-unapplied) and supabase/migrations_backup/20250115000003_event_pages_system.sql. Because the active chain never creates the table, its existence and its RLS policies on any active environment cannot be established from the source of truth, and the application is therefore the only place the disclosure decision can be made. Three independent signals agree: (1) no CREATE TABLE for event_posts exists anywhere under supabase/migrations/; (2) the generated Database types do not contain it, so a scoped tsc of app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts at base SHA reports TS2769 'Argument of type "event_posts" is not assignable to parameter of type ...' at both .from('event_posts') call sites, lines 25 and 125; (3) lib/feed/attending-event-posts.ts and components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx also depend on it. Exact object names: public.event_posts, and its policies 'Users can view public event posts', 'Users can create posts for events they're attending or organizing', 'Users can update their own posts', 'Users can delete their own posts or event organizers can delete any post' as written in the archived file at lines 316, 319, 332 and 335. This is reported, not worked around: EVENTS-004 did not author or apply a migration, did not alter supabase/migrations/**, and applied nothing to any database. The events lane did add an application-layer viewer gate so that the disclosure decision no longer depends on an RLS policy whose existence is unproven; that gate is defence in depth, not a substitute for the schema decision.

completed: COMPLETION CONDITION MET, BRANCH ONE: the additive migration exists. supabase/migrations/20260928010000_event_posts_and_event_claims.sql (sha256 d56fdb54df7fdd347a6b7606191d6a122fe3925a66200e98142acef1e693a636) creates public.event_posts with RLS ENABLED AND FORCED, four policies, explicit grants, and an in-transaction post-condition that asserts the whole contract by name in both directions.

AC-1 disposition: THE CHAIN IS THE ANSWER. No out-of-band artifact is authoritative. The two candidate definitions are supabase/migration-archive/pre-reconciliation-local-only-2026-08-20/20250120000000_event_social_features.sql, whose MANIFEST.csv:2 status is `duplicate_version_noncanonical` in a directory named local-only-unapplied, and supabase/migrations_backup/20250115000003_event_pages_system.sql, a backup copy this repository classifies as evidence only. They are MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE on media_urls (text[] vs jsonb), on type (NOT NULL with 4 literals vs nullable with 6) and on visibility (NOT NULL default 'public' with 3 literals vs nullable default 'attendees' with 3 different literals), and the migrations_backup policy set is not transcribable at all because it references public.events.created_by, public.event_collaborators and public.event_page_settings, none of which any active migration creates, and it ships `GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO authenticated` at line 443. `media_urls` was decided by three independent call sites that write or type a JS string array.

AC-4 analogue for this table: the handoff's warning that transcribing the archived read predicate as-is should be re-examined was correct, and the re-examination went further than expected. The pre-reconciliation read policy (`visibility = 'public' OR auth.uid() = user_id`) is INCOMPATIBLE with the code: it makes the `.in('visibility', ['public','attendees'])` filter in lib/feed/attending-event-posts.ts:220 dead and would show an attendee none of the attendee-visible posts. The installed read is the migrations_backup shape, narrowed by removing its event_collaborators arm, and split into a role-agnostic policy plus an `to authenticated` attendees policy.

Two further divergences forced by live code and recorded rather than copied: event_table now admits 'events_v2', which NEITHER archive admits, without which app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts:143 cannot post on any canonical event; and `author_id uuid` was ADDED, because two live writers write it and it is absent from both archives and from the archive's own missing-column alignment block at :135-175.

THE DISCLOSURE DECISION, now established in the schema rather than only in application code: anon holds SELECT and reads only `visibility = 'public'`; an authenticated caller reads their own rows whatever the visibility; an ATTENDING authenticated caller reads 'attendees' posts for events they are attending. There is NO predicate on the parent event's publication state, so a public post on a draft or cancelled event is anon-readable. That residual is named, not hidden, and routed in HF-DB023-EVENT-POSTS-CALLERS because closing it needs the publication contract for three parent relations.

NOT fixed here, by design: the `profiles:user_id (...)` embed in two routes, the client-side insert in components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx, and the unvalidated `visibility` passthrough. All three are app/ files outside this grant. Routed.
